standard_prerequisites.name: The functor RH^0_T of sections with support in a specialization-stable subset T, defined as the filtered colimit of the functors H^0_Z over closed Z contained in T
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Defined in the author's section on generalities about local cohomology, where the counted statement occurs
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the object whose cohomology the statement computes.

standard_prerequisites.name: K-injective complexes as a model for the derived category, and exactness of filtered colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at source lines 1006-1017
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof represent the derived functor by an explicit complex and commute the colimit with cohomology.

core_obligations: Represent the object: the proof chooses a K-injective complex representing the given object of the derived category (proof lines 1006-1007)

Compute the functor on the complex: by the definition of the functor with support in T, it is represented by the colimit of the complexes of sections with support in the closed subsets of T contained in the subset (proof lines 1007-1012)

Commute colimits with cohomology: since filtered colimits are exact, the cohomology in degree i of that complex is the filtered colimit of the cohomologies of the individual complexes, which is exactly the right-hand side of the statement (proof lines 1013-1017)
Conclusion: the displayed identity of the statement (proof line 1017)
proof_roadmap: 取 K-内射复形代表 K；由 RH^0_T 的定义，它由 H^0_T(J^∙) = colim H^0_Z(J^∙) 表示。
滤过余极限正合，故第 i 个上同调等于 colim H^i(H^0_Z(J^∙)) = colim H^i_Z(K)，即所证。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement identifies the cohomology of the zeroth local cohomology functor along a specialization-stable subset with a filtered colimit of the cohomologies with support in closed subsets (author lemma at source lines 996-1004, label lemma-adjoint-ext). The proof (source lines 1006-1017) is a short but complete computation: it represents the object by a K-injective complex, applies the definition of the functor as a filtered colimit over closed subsets, and uses exactness of filtered colimits to commute the colimit with taking cohomology (proof lines 1013-1017). Every step is written out, and the counted proof contains no cross-reference and no citation. H2.
